8393.text: And Abʹsa·lom would go on to say: “O that I were appointed judge in the land, that to me every man might come that happens to have a legal case or judgment! Then I should certainly do justice to him.”

8394.label: 2 Samuel 15:5
8394.text: It also occurred that, when a man drew near to bow down to him, he thrust his hand out and grabbed hold of him and kissed him.

8395.label: 2 Samuel 15:6
8395.text: And Abʹsa·lom kept doing a thing like this to all Israelites that would come in for judgment to the king; and Abʹsa·lom kept stealing the hearts of the men of Israel.

8396.label: 2 Samuel 15:7
8396.text: And it came about at the end of forty years that Abʹsa·lom proceeded to say to the king: “Let me go, please, and pay in Heʹbron my vow that I solemnly made to Jehovah.

8397.label: 2 Samuel 15:8
8397.text: For your servant made a solemn vow when I was dwelling in Geshʹur in Syria, saying, ‘If Jehovah will without fail bring me back to Jerusalem, I must also render service to Jehovah.’”

8398.label: 2 Samuel 15:9
8398.text: So the king said to him: “Go in peace.” With that he rose up and went to Heʹbron.

8399.label: 2 Samuel 15:10
8399.text: Abʹsa·lom now sent spies through all the tribes of Israel, saying: “As soon as YOU hear the sound of the horn, YOU must also say, ‘Abʹsa·lom has become king in Heʹbron!’”

8400.label: 2 Samuel 15:11
8400.text: Now there had gone with Abʹsa·lom two hundred men from Jerusalem, being called and going unsuspectingly, and they did not know a single thing.

8401.label: 2 Samuel 15:12
8401.text: Further, when he offered the sacrifices, Abʹsa·lom sent for A·hithʹo·phel the Giʹlon·ite, David’s counselor, from his city Giʹloh. And the conspiracy kept getting stronger, and the people were continually growing in number with Abʹsa·lom.

8402.label: 2 Samuel 15:13
8402.text: In time an informer came to David, saying: “The heart of the men of Israel has come to be behind Abʹsa·lom.”

8403.label: 2 Samuel 15:14
8403.text: At once David said to all his servants that were with him in Jerusalem: “Get up, and let us run away; for there will prove to be no escaping for us because of Abʹsa·lom! Go hurriedly, for fear he may hurry up and actually catch up with us and bring down upon us what is bad and strike the city with the edge of the sword!”

8404.label: 2 Samuel 15:15
8404.text: At this the king’s servants said to the king: “According to all that my lord the king may choose, here are your servants.”

8405.label: 2 Samuel 15:16
8405.text: So the king went out with all his household at his feet, and the king left ten women, concubines, to take care of the house.

8406.label: 2 Samuel 15:17
8406.text: And the king continued on his way out with all the people at his feet; and they came to a stop at Beth-merʹhak.

8407.label: 2 Samuel 15:18
8407.text: And all his servants were crossing at his side; and all the Cherʹe·thites and all the Pelʹe·thites and all the Gitʹtites, six hundred men that had followed him from Gath, were crossing before the king’s face.

8408.label: 2 Samuel 15:19
8408.text: Then the king said to Itʹtai the Gitʹtite: “Why should you yourself also go with us? Go back and dwell with the king; for you are a foreigner and, besides, you are an exile from your place.

8409.label: 2 Samuel 15:20
8409.text: Yesterday was when you came and today shall I make you wander with us, to go when I am going wherever I am going? Go back and take your brothers back with you, [and may Jehovah exercise toward you] loving-kindness and trustworthiness!”

8410.label: 2 Samuel 15:21
8410.text: But Itʹtai answered the king and said: “As Jehovah is living and as my lord the king is living, in the place where my lord the king may come to be, whether for death or for life, there is where your servant will come to be!”

8411.label: 2 Samuel 15:22
8411.text: At that David said to Itʹtai: “Go and cross over.” So Itʹtai the Gitʹtite crossed over, and also all his men and all the little ones that were with him.

8412.label: 2 Samuel 15:23
8412.text: And all the people of the land were weeping with a loud voice, and all the people were crossing over, and the king was standing by the torrent valley of Kidʹron, and all the people were crossing over upon the open road to the wilderness.

8413.label: 2 Samuel 15:24
8413.text: And here also there were Zaʹdok and with him all the Levites carrying the ark of the covenant of the [true] God; and they proceeded to set the ark of the [true] God down by A·biʹa·thar until all the people completed crossing over from the city.

8414.label: 2 Samuel 15:25
8414.text: But the king said to Zaʹdok: “Take the ark of the [true] God back to the city. If I shall find favor in the eyes of Jehovah, he will also certainly bring me back and let me see it and its abiding place.

8415.label: 2 Samuel 15:26
8415.text: But if this is what he should say, ‘I have found no delight in you,’ here I am, let him do to me just as it is good in his eyes.”

8416.label: 2 Samuel 15:27
8416.text: And the king went on to say to Zaʹdok the priest: “You are a seer, are you? Do return to the city in peace, and also A·himʹa·az your son and Jonʹa·than the son of A·biʹa·thar, the two sons of YOU men, with YOU.

8417.label: 2 Samuel 15:28
8417.text: See, I am lingering by the fords of the wilderness until word comes from YOU men to inform me.”

8418.label: 2 Samuel 15:29
8418.text: Accordingly Zaʹdok and A·biʹa·thar took the ark of the [true] God back to Jerusalem, and they continued to dwell there.

8419.label: 2 Samuel 15:30
8419.text: And David was going up by the ascent of the Olives, weeping as he went up, with his head covered; and he was walking barefoot, and all the people that were with him covered each one his head, and they went up weeping as they went up.

8420.label: 2 Samuel 15:31
8420.text: And to David the report was made, saying: “A·hithʹo·phel himself is among those conspiring with Abʹsa·lom.” At this David said: “Turn, please, the counsel of A·hithʹo·phel into foolishness, O Jehovah!”

8421.label: 2 Samuel 15:32
8421.text: And it came about that when David himself came to the summit where people used to bow down to God, here to meet him was Huʹshai the Arʹchite, with his robe ripped apart and dirt upon his head.

8422.label: 2 Samuel 15:33
8422.text: However, David said to him: “If you actually went across with me, you would then certainly become a load upon me.

8423.label: 2 Samuel 15:34
8423.text: But if you return to the city and you actually say to Abʹsa·lom, ‘I am your servant, O King. I used to prove myself the servant of your father, even I at that time, but now even I am your servant,’ you must then frustrate the counsel of A·hithʹo·phel for me.

8424.label: 2 Samuel 15:35
8424.text: Are not Zaʹdok and A·biʹa·thar the priests there with you? And it must occur that everything that you may hear from the house of the king you should tell to Zaʹdok and A·biʹa·thar the priests.

8425.label: 2 Samuel 15:36
8425.text: Look! There with them are their two sons, A·himʹa·az belonging to Zaʹdok and Jonʹa·than belonging to A·biʹa·thar; and by means of them YOU men must send to me everything that YOU may hear.”

8426.label: 2 Samuel 15:37
8426.text: So Huʹshai, David’s companion, came into the city. As for Abʹsa·lom, he proceeded to come into Jerusalem.

8427.label: 2 Samuel 16:1
8427.text: When David himself had crossed over a little beyond the summit, there was Ziʹba the attendant of Me·phibʹo·sheth to meet him with a couple of asses saddled and upon them two hundred loaves of bread and a hundred cakes of raisins and a hundred loads of summer fruit and a large jar of wine.

8428.label: 2 Samuel 16:2
8428.text: Then the king said to Ziʹba: “What do these things mean on your part?” To this Ziʹba said: “The asses are for the household of the king to ride, and the bread and the load of summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for the one tired out in the wilderness to drink.”

8429.label: 2 Samuel 16:3
8429.text: The king now said: “And where is the son of your master?” At this Ziʹba said to the king: “There he is dwelling in Jerusalem; for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will give back to me the royal rule of my father.’”

8430.label: 2 Samuel 16:4
8430.text: The king then said to Ziʹba: “Look! Yours is everything that belongs to Me·phibʹo·sheth.” Upon that Ziʹba said: “I do bow down. Let me find favor in your eyes, my lord the king.”

8431.label: 2 Samuel 16:5
8431.text: And King David came as far as Ba·huʹrim, and, look! coming out from there was a man of the family of Saul’s house, and his name was Shimʹe·i, the son of Geʹra, coming out and calling down evil as he came out.

8432.label: 2 Samuel 16:6
8432.text: And he began throwing stones at David and at all the servants of King David; and all the people and all the mighty men were at his right and at his left.

8433.label: 2 Samuel 16:7
8433.text: And this is what Shimʹe·i said as he called down evil: “Get out, get out, you bloodguilty man and good-for-nothing man!

8434.label: 2 Samuel 16:8
8434.text: Jehovah has brought back upon you all the bloodguilt for the house of Saul in place of whom you have ruled as king; and Jehovah gives the kingship into the hand of Abʹsa·lom your son. And here you are in your calamity, because you are a bloodguilty man!”

8435.label: 2 Samuel 16:9
8435.text: Finally A·bishʹai the son of Ze·ruʹiah said to the king: “Why should this dead dog call down evil upon my lord the king? Let me go over, please, and take off his head.”

8436.label: 2 Samuel 16:10
8436.text: But the king said: “What do I have to do with YOU men, YOU sons of Ze·ruʹiah? Thus let him call down evil, because Jehovah himself has said to him, ‘Call down evil upon David!’ So who should say, ‘Why did you do that way?’”

8437.label: 2 Samuel 16:11
8437.text: And David went on to say to A·bishʹai and all his servants: “Here my own son, who has come forth out of my own inward parts, is looking for my soul; and how much more now a Benʹja·min·ite! Let him alone that he may call down evil, for Jehovah has said so to him!

8438.label: 2 Samuel 16:12
8438.text: Perhaps Jehovah will see with his eye, and Jehovah will actually restore to me goodness instead of his malediction this day.”

8439.label: 2 Samuel 16:13
8439.text: With that David and his men kept going on in the road, while Shimʹe·i was walking on the side of the mountain, walking abreast of him that he might call down evil; and he kept throwing stones while abreast of him, and he threw a lot of dust.

8440.label: 2 Samuel 16:14
8440.text: At length the king and all the people that were with him arrived tired. So they refreshed themselves there.

8441.label: 2 Samuel 16:15
8441.text: As for Abʹsa·lom and all the people, the men of Israel, they entered Jerusalem; and A·hithʹo·phel was with him.

8442.label: 2 Samuel 16:16
8442.text: And it came about that, as soon as Huʹshai the Arʹchite, David’s companion, came in to Abʹsa·lom, Huʹshai proceeded to say to Abʹsa·lom: “Let the king live! Let the king live!”

8443.label: 2 Samuel 16:17
8443.text: At this Abʹsa·lom said to Huʹshai: “This is the loving-kindness of yours toward your companion, is it? Why did you not go with your companion?”

8444.label: 2 Samuel 16:18
8444.text: So Huʹshai said to Abʹsa·lom: “No; but the one whom Jehovah has chosen and also this people and all the men of Israel, his I shall become, and with him I shall dwell.

8445.label: 2 Samuel 16:19
8445.text: And for the second time [I must say], Whom shall I myself serve? Is it not before his son? Just as I served before your father, so I shall prove to be before you.”

8446.label: 2 Samuel 16:20
8446.text: Later Abʹsa·lom said to A·hithʹo·phel: “YOU men, give counsel on YOUR part. What shall we do?”

8447.label: 2 Samuel 16:21
8447.text: Then A·hithʹo·phel said to Abʹsa·lom: “Have relations with the concubines of your father, whom he left behind to take care of the house. And all Israel will certainly hear that you have made yourself foul-smelling to your father, and the hands of all those who are with you will certainly become strong.”

8448.label: 2 Samuel 16:22
8448.text: Accordingly they pitched a tent for Abʹsa·lom upon the roof, and Abʹsa·lom began to have relations with the concubines of his father under the eyes of all Israel.

8449.label: 2 Samuel 16:23
8449.text: And the counsel of A·hithʹo·phel, with which he counseled in those days, was just as when a man would inquire of the word of the [true] God. That was the way all the counsel of A·hithʹo·phel was both to David and to Abʹsa·lom.

8450.label: 2 Samuel 17:1
8450.text: And A·hithʹo·phel proceeded to say to Abʹsa·lom: “Let me choose, please, twelve thousand men and rise up and chase after David tonight.

8451.label: 2 Samuel 17:2
8451.text: And I shall come upon him when he is weary and feeble in both hands, and I shall certainly drive him into trembling; and all the people that are with him will have to flee, and I shall certainly strike down the king by himself.

8452.label: 2 Samuel 17:3
8452.text: And let me bring all the people back to you. Equivalent to the returning of all is the man whom you are seeking; [and] all the people will themselves come to be at peace.”

8453.label: 2 Samuel 17:4
8453.text: And the word was just right in the eyes of Abʹsa·lom and in the eyes of all the older men of Israel.

8454.label: 2 Samuel 17:5
8454.text: However, Abʹsa·lom said: “Call, please, Huʹshai the Arʹchite also, and let us hear what is in his mouth, even his.”

8455.label: 2 Samuel 17:6
8455.text: So Huʹshai came in to Abʹsa·lom. Then Abʹsa·lom said to him: “According to this word is the way A·hithʹo·phel spoke. Shall we act upon his word? If not, you yourself speak.”

8456.label: 2 Samuel 17:7
8456.text: At this Huʹshai said to Abʹsa·lom: “The counsel with which A·hithʹo·phel has counseled is not good in this instance!”

8457.label: 2 Samuel 17:8
8457.text: And Huʹshai went on to say: “You yourself well know your father and the men of his, that they are mighty, and they are bitter of soul, like a female bear that has lost her cubs in the field; and your father is a warrior, and he will not spend the night with the people.

8458.label: 2 Samuel 17:9
8458.text: Look! Now he is in hiding in one of the hollows or in one of the other places; and it will certainly occur that, just as soon as he falls upon them at the start, the one hearing of it will then be bound to hear and say, ‘A defeat has taken place among the people that are following Abʹsa·lom!’

8459.label: 2 Samuel 17:10
8459.text: And even the valiant man whose heart is as the heart of the lion will himself surely soften in weakness; for all Israel is aware that your father is a mighty man and so, too, are the valiant men that are with him.

8460.label: 2 Samuel 17:11
8460.text: I myself do say in counsel: Let all Israel without fail be gathered to you, from Dan to Beʹer-sheʹba, as the sand particles that are by the sea for multitude, with your own person going into the fight.

8461.label: 2 Samuel 17:12
8461.text: And we must come against him in one of the places where he is certain to be found, and we ourselves will be upon him just as the dew falls upon the ground; and there will certainly not be left even a single one among him and all the men that are with him.

8462.label: 2 Samuel 17:13
8462.text: And if it is into some city that he will withdraw, all Israel must also carry ropes to that city, and we shall certainly drag it down to the torrent valley, until there shall not be found there even a pebble.”

8463.label: 2 Samuel 17:14
8463.text: Then Abʹsa·lom and all the men of Israel said: “The counsel of Huʹshai the Arʹchite is better than the counsel of A·hithʹo·phel!” And Jehovah himself had given command to frustrate the counsel of A·hithʹo·phel although good, in order that Jehovah might bring calamity upon Abʹsa·lom.

8464.label: 2 Samuel 17:15
8464.text: Later Huʹshai said to Zaʹdok and A·biʹa·thar the priests: “This and that was the way that A·hithʹo·phel counseled Abʹsa·lom and the older men of Israel; and this and that was the way that I myself counseled.

8465.label: 2 Samuel 17:16
8465.text: And now send speedily and tell David, saying, ‘Do not lodge in the desert plains of the wilderness tonight, but you also ought to cross over without fail, for fear that the king and all the people that are with him may be swallowed up.’”

8466.label: 2 Samuel 17:17
8466.text: As Jonʹa·than and A·himʹa·az were standing at En-roʹgel, a maidservant went off and told them. So they themselves went off, as they had to tell King David; for they were not able to appear entering the city.

8467.label: 2 Samuel 17:18
8467.text: However, a young man got to see them and told Abʹsa·lom. So the two of them went off speedily and came to the house of a man in Ba·huʹrim, who had a well in his courtyard; and they went down into it.

8468.label: 2 Samuel 17:19
8468.text: After that the woman took and spread out a screen over the face of the well and heaped up cracked grain upon it; and not a thing became known of it.

8469.label: 2 Samuel 17:20
8469.text: The servants of Abʹsa·lom now came to the woman at her house and said: “Where are A·himʹa·az and Jonʹa·than?” At this the woman said to them: “They passed on from here to the waters.” Then they kept on searching, and they did not find them and so returned to Jerusalem.

8470.label: 2 Samuel 17:21
8470.text: And it came about after their going away that then they came up out of the well and went on and told King David and said to David: “YOU people, rise up and speedily pass over the waters; for this is the way that A·hithʹo·phel counseled against YOU.”

8471.label: 2 Samuel 17:22
8471.text: Immediately David rose up and also all the people that were with him, and they kept crossing the Jordan until the morning became light, until not a one was lacking that had not passed over the Jordan.

8472.label: 2 Samuel 17:23
8472.text: As for A·hithʹo·phel, he saw that his counsel had not been acted upon, and he proceeded to saddle an ass and rise up and go off to his house at his own city. Then he gave commands to his household and strangled himself and thus died. So he was buried in the burial place of his forefathers.

8473.label: 2 Samuel 17:24
8473.text: As for David, he came to Ma·ha·naʹim, and Abʹsa·lom himself crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

8474.label: 2 Samuel 17:25
8474.text: And A·maʹsa was the one whom Abʹsa·lom put in the place of Joʹab over the army; and A·maʹsa was the son of a man whose name was Ithʹra the Israelite, who had relations with Abʹi·gail the daughter of Naʹhash, the sister of Ze·ruʹiah, Joʹab’s mother.

8475.label: 2 Samuel 17:26
8475.text: And Israel and Abʹsa·lom took up camping in the land of Gilʹe·ad.

8476.label: 2 Samuel 17:27
8476.text: And it came about that, as soon as David came to Ma·ha·naʹim, Shoʹbi the son of Naʹhash from Rabʹbah of the sons of Amʹmon, and Maʹchir the son of Amʹmi·el from Lo-deʹbar, and Bar·zilʹlai the Gilʹe·ad·ite from Ro·geʹlim

8477.label: 2 Samuel 17:28
8477.text: [brought] beds and basins and potter’s vessels, and wheat and barley and flour and roasted grain and broad beans and lentils and parched grain;

8478.label: 2 Samuel 17:29
8478.text: and honey and butter and sheep and curds of cattle they brought forward for David and the people that were with him to eat, for they said: “The people are hungry and tired and thirsty in the wilderness.”

8479.label: 2 Samuel 18:1
8479.text: And David proceeded to number the people that were with him and to place over them chiefs of thousands and chiefs of hundreds.

8480.label: 2 Samuel 18:2
8480.text: Further, David sent one third of the people under the hand of Joʹab and one third under the hand of A·bishʹai the son of Ze·ruʹiah, Joʹab’s brother, and one third under the hand of Itʹtai the Gitʹtite. Then the king said to the people: “I myself also shall without fail go out with YOU.”

8481.label: 2 Samuel 18:3
8481.text: But the people said: “You must not go out, for if we should at all flee, they would not set heart upon us; and if half of us would die, they would not set heart upon us, because you are worth ten thousand of us; and now it would be better if you would be of service to us to give help from the city.”

8482.label: 2 Samuel 18:4
8482.text: So the king said to them: “Whatever seems good in YOUR eyes I shall do.” And the king kept standing at the side of the gate, and all the people themselves went out by hundreds and by thousands.

8483.label: 2 Samuel 18:5
8483.text: And the king went on to command Joʹab and A·bishʹai and Itʹtai, saying: “Deal gently for my sake with the young man Abʹsa·lom.” And all the people themselves heard when the king commanded all the chiefs over the matter of Abʹsa·lom.

8484.label: 2 Samuel 18:6
8484.text: And the people continued on their way out to the field to meet Israel; and the battle came to be in the forest of Eʹphra·im.

8485.label: 2 Samuel 18:7
8485.text: Finally the people of Israel were defeated there before the servants of David, and the slaughter there turned out to be great on that day, of twenty thousand men.

8486.label: 2 Samuel 18:8
8486.text: And the battle there got to be spread out over all the land that was in sight. Furthermore, the forest did more in eating up the people than the sword did in eating them up on that day.

8487.label: 2 Samuel 18:9
8487.text: Eventually Abʹsa·lom found himself before the servants of David. And Abʹsa·lom was riding upon a mule, and the mule got to come under the network of boughs of a massive big tree, so that his head got caught fast in the big tree, and he was taken up between the heavens and the earth, as the mule itself that was under him passed along.

8488.label: 2 Samuel 18:10
8488.text: Then a certain man saw it and told Joʹab and said: “Look! I have seen Abʹsa·lom hung in a big tree.”

8489.label: 2 Samuel 18:11
8489.text: At this Joʹab said to the man who was telling him: “And here you saw it, and why did you not strike him down to the earth there? Then it would have been my obligation to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt.”

8490.label: 2 Samuel 18:12
8490.text: But the man said to Joʹab: “And although I were weighing upon my palms a thousand pieces of silver, I should not thrust my hand out against the king’s son; for in our hearing it was that the king commanded you and A·bishʹai and Itʹtai, saying, ‘WATCH, whoever [you are], over the young man, over Abʹsa·lom.’

8491.label: 2 Samuel 18:13
8491.text: Otherwise I should have dealt treacherously against his soul and the whole matter itself would not be hidden from the king, and you yourself would take a position off on the side.”

8492.label: 2 Samuel 18:14
8492.text: To this Joʹab said: “Let me not hold myself up this way before you!” With that he took three shafts in his palm and proceeded to drive them through the heart of Abʹsa·lom while he was yet alive in the heart of the big tree.

8493.label: 2 Samuel 18:15
8493.text: Then ten attendants carrying Joʹab’s weapons came around and struck Abʹsa·lom, that they might put him to death.

8494.label: 2 Samuel 18:16
8494.text: Joʹab now blew the horn, that the people might return from chasing after Israel; for Joʹab had held back the people.

8495.label: 2 Samuel 18:17
8495.text: Finally they took Abʹsa·lom and pitched him in the forest into a big hollow and raised up over him a very big pile of stones. As for all Israel, they fled each man to his home.

8496.label: 2 Samuel 18:18
8496.text: Now Abʹsa·lom himself, while he was alive, had taken and proceeded to raise up for himself a pillar, which is in the Low Plain of the King, for he said: “I have no son in order to keep my name in remembrance.” So he called the pillar by his own name, and it continues to be called Abʹsa·lom’s Monument down to this day.

8497.label: 2 Samuel 18:19
8497.text: Now as regards A·himʹa·az the son of Zaʹdok, he said: “Let me run, please, and break the news to the king, because Jehovah has judged him [to free him] from the hand of his enemies.”

8498.label: 2 Samuel 18:20
8498.text: But Joʹab said to him: “You are not a man of news this day, and you must break the news on another day; but this day you must not break the news, for the very reason that the king’s own son has died.”

8499.label: 2 Samuel 18:21
8499.text: Then Joʹab said to the Cushʹite: “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” At that the Cushʹite bowed to Joʹab and began to run.

8500.label: 2 Samuel 18:22
8500.text: A·himʹa·az the son of Zaʹdok now said once again to Joʹab: “Let, now, happen whatever will, let me also myself, please, run behind the Cushʹite.” However, Joʹab said: “Why is it that you yourself have to run, my son, when there is no news being found for you?”

8501.label: 2 Samuel 18:23
8501.text: [Still he said:] “Let, now, happen whatever will, let me run.” So he said to him: “Run!” And A·himʹa·az began to run by the way of the District, and he eventually passed by the Cushʹite.

8502.label: 2 Samuel 18:24
8502.text: Now David was sitting between the two gates. Meantime, the watchman went to the roof of the gate by the wall. At length he raised his eyes and saw and, look! there was a man running by himself.

8503.label: 2 Samuel 18:25
8503.text: So the watchman called and told the king, at which the king said: “If he is by himself, there is news in his mouth.” And he kept coming, steadily getting nearer.

8504.label: 2 Samuel 18:26
8504.text: The watchman now saw another man running. The watchman therefore called to the gatekeeper and said: “Look! Another man running by himself!” at which the king said: “This one also is a news bearer.”

8505.label: 2 Samuel 18:27
8505.text: And the watchman went on to say: “I am seeing that the running style of the first is like the running style of A·himʹa·az the son of Zaʹdok,” at which the king said: “This is a good man, and with good news he should come.”

8506.label: 2 Samuel 18:28
8506.text: Eventually A·himʹa·az called and said to the king: “It is well!” With that he bowed to the king with his face to the earth. And he went on to say: “Blessed be Jehovah your God, who has surrendered the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king!”

8507.label: 2 Samuel 18:29
8507.text: However, the king said: “Is it well with the young man Abʹsa·lom?” To this A·himʹa·az said: “I saw the great commotion at the time Joʹab sent the king’s servant and your servant, and I did not know what it was.”

8508.label: 2 Samuel 18:30
8508.text: So the king said: “Step aside, take your position here.” At that he stepped aside and kept standing still.

8509.label: 2 Samuel 18:31
8509.text: And here was the Cushʹite coming in, and the Cushʹite began to say: “Let my lord the king accept news, for Jehovah has judged you today [to free you] from the hand of all those rising up against you.”

8510.label: 2 Samuel 18:32
8510.text: But the king said to the Cushʹite: “Is it well with the young man Abʹsa·lom?” To this the Cushʹite said: “May the enemies of my lord the king and all those who rose up against you for evil become as the young man.”

8511.label: 2 Samuel 18:33
8511.text: Then the king became disturbed and went up to the roof chamber over the gateway and gave way to weeping; and this is what he said as he walked: “My son Abʹsa·lom, my son, my son Abʹsa·lom! O that I might have died, I myself, instead of you, Abʹsa·lom my son, my son!”

8512.label: 2 Samuel 19:1
8512.text: Later it was reported to Joʹab: “Look! The king is weeping, and he carries on mourning over Abʹsa·lom.”

8513.label: 2 Samuel 19:2
8513.text: So the salvation on that day came to be an occasion of mourning on the part of all the people, because the people heard say on that day: “The king has felt hurt over his son.”

8514.label: 2 Samuel 19:3
8514.text: And the people began to steal away on that day to come into the city, just as the people would steal away when they felt disgraced because they fled in the battle.

8515.label: 2 Samuel 19:4
8515.text: And the king himself covered up his face, and the king continued crying out with a loud voice: “My son Abʹsa·lom! Abʹsa·lom my son, my son!”

8516.label: 2 Samuel 19:5
8516.text: Finally Joʹab came in to the king at the house and said: “You have today put to shame the face of all your servants, the ones providing escape for your soul today and for the soul of your sons and your daughters and the soul of your wives and the soul of your concubines,

8517.label: 2 Samuel 19:6
8517.text: by loving those hating you and by hating those loving you; for you have reported today that chiefs and servants are nothing to you, because I well know today that if only Abʹsa·lom were alive and all of us others were today dead, why, in that case it would be right in your eyes.

8518.label: 2 Samuel 19:7
8518.text: And now rise up, go out and speak straight to the heart of your servants, because, by Jehovah, I do swear that, in case you are not going out, not a man will lodge with you tonight; and this will certainly be worse for you than all the injury that has come upon you from your youth until now.”

8519.label: 2 Samuel 19:8
8519.text: Accordingly the king rose up and seated himself in the gate, and to all the people they made the report, saying: “There is the king sitting in the gate.” And all the people began to come before the king. As for Israel, they had fled each one to his home.

8520.label: 2 Samuel 19:9
8520.text: And all the people came to be involved in dispute in all the tribes of Israel, saying: “It was the king that delivered us out of the palm of our enemies, and he it was that provided escape for us out of the palm of the Phi·lisʹtines; and now he has run away out of the land from Abʹsa·lom.

8521.label: 2 Samuel 19:10
8521.text: As for Abʹsa·lom, whom we anointed over us, he has died in the battle. So now why are YOU doing nothing to bring the king back?”

8522.label: 2 Samuel 19:11
8522.text: As for King David, he sent to Zaʹdok and A·biʹa·thar the priests, saying: “SPEAK to the older men of Judah, saying, ‘Why should YOU become the last ones to bring the king back to his house, when the word of all Israel itself has come to the king at his house?

8523.label: 2 Samuel 19:12
8523.text: My brothers YOU are; my bone and my flesh YOU are. So why should YOU become the last ones to bring the king back?’

8524.label: 2 Samuel 19:13
8524.text: And to A·maʹsa YOU should say, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? So may God do to me and so may he add to it if you will not become the army chief before me always instead of Joʹab.’”

8525.label: 2 Samuel 19:14
8525.text: And he proceeded to bend the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, so that they sent word to the king: “Come back, you and all your servants.”

8526.label: 2 Samuel 19:15
8526.text: And the king began to go back and got to come as far as the Jordan. As for Judah, they came to Gilʹgal to go and meet the king, to conduct the king across the Jordan.

8527.label: 2 Samuel 19:16
8527.text: Then Shimʹe·i the son of Geʹra the Benʹja·min·ite, who was from Ba·huʹrim, hurried and went down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

8528.label: 2 Samuel 19:17
8528.text: And there were with him a thousand men from Benjamin. (And also Ziʹba the attendant of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants of his were with him, and they made it successfully to the Jordan before the king.

8529.label: 2 Samuel 19:18
8529.text: And he crossed the ford to conduct the household of the king across and to do what was good in his eyes.) As for Shimʹe·i the son of Geʹra, he fell down before the king when he was about to cross the Jordan.

8530.label: 2 Samuel 19:19
8530.text: He now said to the king: “Do not let my lord attribute error to me, and do not remember the wrong that your servant did on the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, so that the king should lay it to his heart.

8531.label: 2 Samuel 19:20
8531.text: For your servant well knows that I am the one that sinned; and so here I have today come the first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.”

8532.label: 2 Samuel 19:21
8532.text: At once A·bishʹai the son of Ze·ruʹiah answered and said: “In return for this should not Shimʹe·i be put to death, in that he called evil down upon the anointed of Jehovah?”

8533.label: 2 Samuel 19:22
8533.text: But David said: “What do I have to do with YOU men, you sons of Ze·ruʹiah, that YOU should become today a resister of me? Will anyone today be put to death in Israel? For do I not well know that today I am king over Israel?”

8534.label: 2 Samuel 19:23
8534.text: Then the king said to Shimʹe·i: “You will not die.” And the king went on to swear to him.

8535.label: 2 Samuel 19:24
8535.text: As for Me·phibʹo·sheth the grandson of Saul, he came down to meet the king; and he had not attended to his feet nor had he attended to his mustache nor had he washed his garments from the day that the king went away until the day that he came in peace.

8536.label: 2 Samuel 19:25
8536.text: And it came about that, when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, then the king said to him: “Why did you not go with me, Me·phibʹo·sheth?”

8537.label: 2 Samuel 19:26
8537.text: To this he said: “My lord the king, it was my servant that tricked me. For your servant had said, ‘Let me saddle the female ass for me that I may ride upon it and go with the king,’ for your servant is lame.

8538.label: 2 Samuel 19:27
8538.text: So he slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is as an angel of the [true] God, and so do what is good in your eyes.

8539.label: 2 Samuel 19:28
8539.text: For all the household of my father would have become nothing but doomed to death to my lord the king, and yet you placed your servant among those eating at your table. So what do I still have as a just claim even for crying out further to the king?”

8540.label: 2 Samuel 19:29
8540.text: However, the king said to him: “Why do you yet keep speaking your words? I do say, You and Ziʹba should share in the field.”

8541.label: 2 Samuel 19:30
8541.text: At this Me·phibʹo·sheth said to the king: “Let him even take the whole, now that my lord the king has come in peace to his house.”

8542.label: 2 Samuel 19:31
8542.text: And Bar·zilʹlai the Gilʹe·ad·ite himself came down from Ro·geʹlim that he might pass on to the Jordan with the king so as to escort him to the Jordan.

8543.label: 2 Samuel 19:32
8543.text: And Bar·zilʹlai was very old, being eighty years of age; and he himself supplied the king with food while he was dwelling in Ma·ha·naʹim, for he was a very great man.

8544.label: 2 Samuel 19:33
8544.text: So the king said to Bar·zilʹlai: “You yourself cross over with me, and I shall certainly supply you with food with me in Jerusalem.”

8545.label: 2 Samuel 19:34
8545.text: But Bar·zilʹlai said to the king: “What are the days of the years of my life like, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

8546.label: 2 Samuel 19:35
8546.text: I am eighty years old today. Could I discern between good and bad, or could your servant taste what I ate and what I drank, or could I listen anymore to the voice of male and female singers? So why should your servant become a burden anymore to my lord the king?

8547.label: 2 Samuel 19:36
8547.text: For it is just a little way that your servant could bring the king along to the Jordan, and why should the king repay me with this reward?

8548.label: 2 Samuel 19:37
8548.text: Let your servant return, please, and let me die in my city close by the burial place of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Chimʹham. Let him cross over with my lord the king; and you do to him what is good in your eyes.”

8549.label: 2 Samuel 19:38
8549.text: Accordingly the king said: “With me Chimʹham will go across, and I myself shall do to him what is good in your eyes; and all that you may choose [to lay] upon me I shall do for you.”

8550.label: 2 Samuel 19:39
8550.text: All the people now began to cross the Jordan, and the king himself crossed; but the king kissed Bar·zilʹlai and blessed him, after which he returned to his place.

8551.label: 2 Samuel 19:40
8551.text: When the king went across to Gilʹgal, Chimʹham himself crossed with him, and also all the people of Judah, and also half the people of Israel, that they might bring the king across.

8552.label: 2 Samuel 19:41
8552.text: And, look! all the men of Israel were coming to the king, and they proceeded to say to the king: “Why did our brothers the men of Judah steal you that they might bring the king and his household and all the men of David with him over the Jordan?”

8553.label: 2 Samuel 19:42
8553.text: At this all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel: “Because the king is closely related to us; and why is it that you have become angry over this thing? Have we eaten at all at the king’s expense, or has a gift been carried to us?”

8554.label: 2 Samuel 19:43
8554.text: However, the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said: “We have ten parts in the king, so that even in David we are more than you. Why, then, have you treated us with contempt, and why did not our matter become first for us to bring our king back?” But the word of the men of Judah was more severe than the word of the men of Israel.

8555.label: 2 Samuel 20:1
8555.text: Now there happened to be there a good-for-nothing man, whose name was Sheʹba, the son of Bichʹri a Benʹja·min·ite; and he proceeded to blow the horn and say: “We have no share in David, and we have no inheritance in the son of Jesʹse. Every one to his gods, O Israel!”

8556.label: 2 Samuel 20:2
8556.text: At that all the men of Israel began to go up from following David to follow Sheʹba the son of Bichʹri; but as for the men of Judah, they stuck to their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

8557.label: 2 Samuel 20:3
8557.text: Eventually David came to his house at Jerusalem. Then the king took the ten women, the concubines whom he had left behind to take care of the house, and he put them in a house of confinement, but he kept on supplying food to them. And with them he did not have any relations, but they continued shut up closely until the day of their dying, in a widowhood with a living [husband].

8558.label: 2 Samuel 20:4
8558.text: The king now said to A·maʹsa: “Call the men of Judah together to me within three days, and you yourself stand here.”

8559.label: 2 Samuel 20:5
8559.text: So A·maʹsa went to call Judah together; but he came later than the fixed time that he had appointed for him.

8560.label: 2 Samuel 20:6
8560.text: Then David said to A·bishʹai: “Now Sheʹba the son of Bichʹri will be worse for us than Abʹsa·lom. You yourself take the servants of your lord and chase after him, that he may not actually find for himself fortified cities and escape before our eyes.”

8561.label: 2 Samuel 20:7
8561.text: Accordingly the men of Joʹab and the Cherʹe·thites and the Pelʹe·thites and all the mighty men went out after him; and they went on out of Jerusalem to chase after Sheʹba the son of Bichʹri.

8562.label: 2 Samuel 20:8
8562.text: They were close by the great stone that is in Gibʹe·on, and A·maʹsa himself came to meet them. Now Joʹab was girded, clothed with a garment; and upon him there was girded a sword attached to his hip, in its sheath. And he himself came forth, and so it fell out.

8563.label: 2 Samuel 20:9
8563.text: And Joʹab proceeded to say to A·maʹsa: “Is it all right with you, my brother?” Then Joʹab’s right hand took hold of A·maʹsa’s beard so as to kiss him.

8564.label: 2 Samuel 20:10
8564.text: As for A·maʹsa, he was not on guard against the sword that was in Joʹab’s hand; so that he struck him with it in the abdomen, and his intestines spilled out to the earth, and he did not have to do it to him again. So he died. And Joʹab and A·bishʹai his brother, for their part, chased after Sheʹba the son of Bichʹri.

8565.label: 2 Samuel 20:11
8565.text: And a certain one of Joʹab’s young men stood over him and kept saying: “Whoever has found delight in Joʹab and whoever belongs to David, let him follow Joʹab!”

8566.label: 2 Samuel 20:12
8566.text: All the while A·maʹsa was wallowing in the blood in the middle of the highway. When the man saw that all the people stood still, then he moved A·maʹsa from the highway to the field. Finally he cast a garment over him, as he saw that everyone coming up to him stood still.

8567.label: 2 Samuel 20:13
8567.text: As soon as he had removed him from the highway, each man passed by following Joʹab to chase after Sheʹba the son of Bichʹri.

8568.label: 2 Samuel 20:14
8568.text: And [Sheʹba] went passing through all the tribes of Israel to Abel of Beth-maʹa·cah. As for all the Bichʹrites, they then congregated together and also went in after him.

8569.label: 2 Samuel 20:15
8569.text: And they proceeded to come and lay siege against him in Abel of Beth-maʹa·cah and cast up a siege rampart against the city, as it was standing within a rampart. And all the people that were with Joʹab were undermining the wall, to throw it down.

8570.label: 2 Samuel 20:16
8570.text: And a wise woman began to call from the city: “Listen, men, listen! Say, please, to Joʹab, ‘Come near as far as here, and let me speak to you.’”

8571.label: 2 Samuel 20:17
8571.text: So he went near to her, and the woman then said: “Are you Joʹab?” to which he said: “I am.” At this she said to him: “Listen to the words of your slave girl.” In turn he said: “I am listening.”

8572.label: 2 Samuel 20:18
8572.text: And she went on to say: “Without exception they used to speak in former times, saying, ‘Let them but inquire in Abel, and thus they will certainly end the matter.’

8573.label: 2 Samuel 20:19
8573.text: I represent the peaceable and faithful ones of Israel. You are seeking to put to death a city and a mother in Israel. Why should you swallow up the inheritance of Jehovah?”

8574.label: 2 Samuel 20:20
8574.text: To this Joʹab answered and said: “It is altogether unthinkable on my part that I should swallow up and that I should bring to ruin.

8575.label: 2 Samuel 20:21
8575.text: The matter is not that way, but a man from the mountainous region of Eʹphra·im, whose name is Sheʹba the son of Bichʹri, has lifted up his hand against King David. YOU people, give him over by himself, and I will withdraw from the city.” Then the woman said to Joʹab: “Look! His head [will be] pitched to you over the wall!”

8576.label: 2 Samuel 20:22
8576.text: At once the woman went in her wisdom to all the people, and they proceeded to cut off the head of Sheʹba the son of Bichʹri and pitch it to Joʹab. Upon that he blew the horn, and so they were scattered from the city, each one to his home; and Joʹab himself returned to Jerusalem to the king.

8577.label: 2 Samuel 20:23
8577.text: And Joʹab was over all the army of Israel; and Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da was over the Cherʹe·thites and over the Pelʹe·thites.

8578.label: 2 Samuel 20:24
8578.text: And A·doʹram was over those conscripted for forced labor; and Je·hoshʹa·phat the son of A·hiʹlud was the recorder.

8579.label: 2 Samuel 20:25
8579.text: And Sheʹva was secretary, and Zaʹdok and A·biʹa·thar were priests.

8580.label: 2 Samuel 20:26
8580.text: And Iʹra the Jaʹir·ite also became a priest of David.

8581.label: 2 Samuel 21:1
8581.text: Now there came to be a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year; and David proceeded to consult the face of Jehovah. Then Jehovah said: “Upon Saul and upon his house there is bloodguilt, because he put the Gibʹe·on·ites to death.”

8582.label: 2 Samuel 21:2
8582.text: So the king called the Gibʹe·on·ites and talked to them. (Incidentally, the Gibʹe·on·ites were not of the sons of Israel, but of the remainder of the Amʹor·ites; and the sons of Israel themselves had sworn to them, but Saul sought to strike them down in his feeling jealous for the sons of Israel and Judah.)

8583.label: 2 Samuel 21:3
8583.text: And David went on to say to the Gibʹe·on·ites: “What shall I do to YOU, and with what shall I make atonement, that YOU may certainly bless the inheritance of Jehovah?”

8584.label: 2 Samuel 21:4
8584.text: So the Gibʹe·on·ites said to him: “It is not a matter of silver or gold for us in connection with Saul and his household, neither is it ours to put a man to death in Israel.” At that he said: “Whatever YOU are saying I shall do for YOU.”

8585.label: 2 Samuel 21:5
8585.text: At this they said to the king: “The man that exterminated us and that schemed to annihilate us from subsisting in any of the territory of Israel,

8586.label: 2 Samuel 21:6
8586.text: let there be given to us seven men of his sons; and we must expose them to Jehovah in Gibʹe·ah of Saul, the chosen one of Jehovah.” Accordingly the king said: “I myself shall give them.”

8587.label: 2 Samuel 21:7
8587.text: However, the king felt compassion upon Me·phibʹo·sheth the son of Jonʹa·than the son of Saul on account of the oath of Jehovah that was between them, between David and Jonʹa·than the son of Saul.

8588.label: 2 Samuel 21:8
8588.text: Consequently the king took the two sons of Rizʹpah the daughter of Aʹiah whom she bore to Saul, Ar·moʹni and Me·phibʹo·sheth, and the five sons of Miʹchal the daughter of Saul whom she bore to Aʹdri·el the son of Bar·zilʹlai the Me·holʹath·ite.

8589.label: 2 Samuel 21:9
8589.text: Then he gave them into the hand of the Gibʹe·on·ites and they proceeded to expose them on the mountain before Jehovah, so that the seven of them fell together; and they themselves were put to death in the first days of harvest, at the start of the barley harvest.

8590.label: 2 Samuel 21:10
8590.text: However, Rizʹpah the daughter of Aʹiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself upon the rock from the start of harvest until water poured down upon them from the heavens; and she did not allow the fowls of the heavens to rest upon them by day nor the wild beasts of the field by night.

8591.label: 2 Samuel 21:11
8591.text: At length it was reported to David what Rizʹpah the daughter of Aʹiah, Saul’s concubine, had done.

8592.label: 2 Samuel 21:12
8592.text: So David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonʹa·than his son from the landowners of Jaʹbesh-gilʹe·ad, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan, where the Phi·lisʹtines had hanged them on the day that the Phi·lisʹtines struck down Saul on Gil·boʹa.

8593.label: 2 Samuel 21:13
8593.text: And he proceeded to bring up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonʹa·than his son; furthermore, they gathered the bones of the men being exposed.

8594.label: 2 Samuel 21:14
8594.text: Then they buried the bones of Saul and of Jonʹa·than his son in the land of Benjamin in Zeʹla in the burial place of Kish his father, that they might do everything that the king had commanded. So God let himself be entreated for the land after this.

8595.label: 2 Samuel 21:15
8595.text: And the Phi·lisʹtines came to have war again with Israel. Accordingly David and his servants with him went down and fought the Phi·lisʹtines; and David grew tired.

8596.label: 2 Samuel 21:16
8596.text: And Ishʹbi-beʹnob, who was among those born of the Rephʹa·im, the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of copper and who was girded with a new sword, got to think of striking David down.

8597.label: 2 Samuel 21:17
8597.text: At once A·bishʹai the son of Ze·ruʹiah came to his help and struck the Phi·lisʹtine down and put him to death. At that time the men of David swore to him, saying: “You must not go out with us to the battle anymore, that you may not extinguish the lamp of Israel!”

8598.label: 2 Samuel 21:18
8598.text: And it came about after this that war arose once more with the Phi·lisʹtines at Gob. Then it was that Sibʹbe·cai the Huʹshath·ite struck down Saph, who was among those born of the Rephʹa·im.

8599.label: 2 Samuel 21:19
8599.text: And war arose once again with the Phi·lisʹtines at Gob, and El·haʹnan the son of Jaʹa·re-orʹe·gim the Bethʹle·hem·ite got to strike down Go·liʹath the Gitʹtite, the shaft of whose spear was like the beam of loom workers.

8600.label: 2 Samuel 21:20
8600.text: And war arose yet again at Gath, when there happened to be a man of extraordinary size, with six fingers on each of his hands and six toes on each of his feet, twenty-four in number; and he too had been born to the Rephʹa·im.

8601.label: 2 Samuel 21:21
8601.text: And he kept taunting Israel. Finally Jonʹa·than the son of Shimʹe·i, David’s brother, struck him down.

8602.label: 2 Samuel 21:22
8602.text: These four had been born to the Rephʹa·im in Gath; and they came to fall by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

8603.label: 2 Samuel 22:1
8603.text: And David proceeded to speak to Jehovah the words of this song in the day that Jehovah had delivered him out of the palm of all his enemies and out of Saul’s palm;

8604.label: 2 Samuel 22:2
8604.text: and he went on to say: “Jehovah is my crag and my stronghold and the Provider of escape for me.

8605.label: 2 Samuel 22:3
8605.text: My God is my rock. I shall take refuge in him,My shield and my horn of salvation, my secure height, And my place for flight, my Savior; from violence you save me.

8606.label: 2 Samuel 22:4
8606.text: On the One to be praised, Jehovah, I shall call,And from my enemies I shall be saved.

8607.label: 2 Samuel 22:5
8607.text: For deadly breaking waves encircled me; There were flash floods of good-for-nothing [men] that kept terrifying me.

8608.label: 2 Samuel 22:6
8608.text: The ropes of Sheʹol themselves surrounded me; The snares of death confronted me.

8609.label: 2 Samuel 22:7
8609.text: In my distress I kept calling upon Jehovah, And to my God I kept calling. Then out of his temple he heard my voice, With my cry for help in his ears.

8610.label: 2 Samuel 22:8
8610.text: And back and forth the earth began to shake and to rock; The foundations of the heavens themselves became agitated, And they kept shaking back and forth because he had been angered.

8611.label: 2 Samuel 22:9
8611.text: Smoke went up at his nostrils, and fire itself from his mouth kept devouring; Coals themselves blazed up from him.

8612.label: 2 Samuel 22:10
8612.text: And he proceeded to bend the heavens down and to descend; And thick gloom was beneath his feet.

8613.label: 2 Samuel 22:11
8613.text: And he came riding upon a cherub and came flying;And he was visible upon the wings of a spirit.

8614.label: 2 Samuel 22:12
8614.text: Then he put a darkness around him as booths, Dark waters, thick clouds.

8615.label: 2 Samuel 22:13
8615.text: From the brightness in front of him burning coals of fire blazed up.

8616.label: 2 Samuel 22:14
8616.text: From heaven Jehovah began to thunder, And the Most High himself began to give forth his voice.

8617.label: 2 Samuel 22:15
8617.text: And he kept sending out arrows, that he might scatter them; Lightning, that he might throw them into confusion.

8618.label: 2 Samuel 22:16
8618.text: And the streambeds of the sea became visible, The foundations of the productive land became uncovered,At the rebuke of Jehovah, from the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

8619.label: 2 Samuel 22:17
8619.text: He was sending from on high, he was taking me, He was drawing me out of great waters.

8620.label: 2 Samuel 22:18
8620.text: He was delivering me from my strong enemy, From those hating me; because they were stronger than I was.

8621.label: 2 Samuel 22:19
8621.text: They kept confronting me in the day of my disaster, But Jehovah became my support.

8622.label: 2 Samuel 22:20
8622.text: And he proceeded to bring me out into a roomy place; He was rescuing me, because he had found delight in me.

8623.label: 2 Samuel 22:21
8623.text: Jehovah rewards me according to my righteousness; According to the cleanness of my hands he repays me.

8624.label: 2 Samuel 22:22
8624.text: For I have kept the ways of Jehovah, And I have not wickedly departed from my God.

8625.label: 2 Samuel 22:23
8625.text: For all his judicial decisions are in front of me;And as for his statutes, I shall not turn aside from them.

8626.label: 2 Samuel 22:24
8626.text: And I shall prove myself faultless toward him,And I will keep myself from error on my part.

8627.label: 2 Samuel 22:25
8627.text: And let Jehovah repay me according to my righteousness, According to my cleanness in front of his eyes.

8628.label: 2 Samuel 22:26
8628.text: With someone loyal you will act in loyalty; With the faultless, mighty one you will deal faultlessly;

8629.label: 2 Samuel 22:27
8629.text: With the one keeping clean you will show yourself clean, And with the crooked one you will act as silly.

8630.label: 2 Samuel 22:28
8630.text: And the humble people you will save; But your eyes are against the haughty ones, [that] you may bring [them] low.

8631.label: 2 Samuel 22:29
8631.text: For you are my lamp, O Jehovah, And it is Jehovah that makes my darkness shine.

8632.label: 2 Samuel 22:30
8632.text: For by you I can run against a marauder band; By my God I can climb a wall.

8633.label: 2 Samuel 22:31
8633.text: As for the [true] God, perfect is his way; The saying of Jehovah is a refined one. A shield he is to all those taking refuge in him.

8634.label: 2 Samuel 22:32
8634.text: For who is a God besides Jehovah, And who is a rock besides our God?

8635.label: 2 Samuel 22:33
8635.text: The [true] God is my strong fortress, And he will cause my way to be perfect,

8636.label: 2 Samuel 22:34
8636.text: Making my feet like those of the hinds; And upon places high for me he keeps me standing.

8637.label: 2 Samuel 22:35
8637.text: He is teaching my hands for warfare; And my arms have pressed down a bow of copper.

8638.label: 2 Samuel 22:36
8638.text: And you will give me your shield of salvation, And it is your humility that makes me great.

8639.label: 2 Samuel 22:37
8639.text: You will make room large enough for my steps under me; And my ankles will certainly not wobble.

8640.label: 2 Samuel 22:38
8640.text: I will pursue my enemies, that I may annihilate them,And I shall not return until they are exterminated.

8641.label: 2 Samuel 22:39
8641.text: And I shall exterminate them and break them in pieces, that they may not rise up; And they will fall under my feet.

8642.label: 2 Samuel 22:40
8642.text: And you will gird me with vital energy for the battle; You will make those rising against me collapse under me.

8643.label: 2 Samuel 22:41
8643.text: And as for my enemies, you will certainly give me the back of their neck; Those hating me intensely—I shall also silence them.

8644.label: 2 Samuel 22:42
8644.text: They cry for help, but there is no savior; To Jehovah, but he actually does not answer them.

8645.label: 2 Samuel 22:43
8645.text: And I shall pound them fine like the dust of the earth;Like the mire of the streets I shall pulverize them; I shall beat them flat.

8646.label: 2 Samuel 22:44
8646.text: And you will provide me escape from the faultfinding of my people. You will safeguard me to be the head of nations; A people that I have not known—they will serve me.

8647.label: 2 Samuel 22:45
8647.text: Foreigners themselves will come cringing to me; Ears will be obedient to hear me.

8648.label: 2 Samuel 22:46
8648.text: Foreigners themselves will fade away,And they will come quaking out from their bulwarks.

8649.label: 2 Samuel 22:47
8649.text: Jehovah is living; and blessed be my Rock; And let the God of the rock of my salvation be exalted.

8650.label: 2 Samuel 22:48
8650.text: The [true] God is the Giver of acts of vengeance to me And the One bringing the peoples down under me,

8651.label: 2 Samuel 22:49
8651.text: And the One bringing me out from my enemies. And above those who rise up against me you will lift me up; From the man of violent deeds you will deliver me.

8652.label: 2 Samuel 22:50
8652.text: That is why I shall thank you, O Jehovah, among the nations; And to your name I shall make melody:

8653.label: 2 Samuel 22:51
8653.text: The One doing great acts of salvation for his king And exercising loving-kindness to his anointed one, To David and to his seed for time indefinite.”

8654.label: 2 Samuel 23:1
8654.text: And these are the last words of David: “The utterance of David the son of Jesʹse, And the utterance of the able-bodied man that was raised up on high, The anointed of the God of Jacob,And the pleasant one of the melodies of Israel.

8655.label: 2 Samuel 23:2
8655.text: The spirit of Jehovah it was that spoke by me, And his word was upon my tongue.

8656.label: 2 Samuel 23:3
8656.text: The God of Israel said,To me the Rock of Israel spoke, ‘When one ruling over mankind is righteous, Ruling in the fear of God,

8657.label: 2 Samuel 23:4
8657.text: Then it is as the light of morning, when the sun shines forth, A morning without clouds.From brightness, from rain, there is grass out of the earth.’

8658.label: 2 Samuel 23:5
8658.text: For is not my household like that with God? Because it is an indefinitely lasting covenant that he has assigned to me,Nicely put in order in everything and secured. Because it is all my salvation and all my delight,Is that not why he will make it grow?

8659.label: 2 Samuel 23:6
8659.text: But good-for-nothing persons are chased away, like thornbushes, all of them;For it is not by the hand that they should be taken.

8660.label: 2 Samuel 23:7
8660.text: When a man touches themHe should be fully armed with iron and the shaft of a spear,And with fire they will thoroughly be burned up.”

8661.label: 2 Samuel 23:8
8661.text: These are the names of the mighty men that belonged to David: Joʹsheb-bas·sheʹbeth a Tah·cheʹmo·nite, the head of the three. He was brandishing his spear over eight hundred slain at one time.

8662.label: 2 Samuel 23:9
8662.text: Next to him El·e·aʹzar the son of Doʹdo the son of A·hoʹhi was among the three mighty men with David when they taunted the Phi·lisʹtines. They had gathered themselves there for the battle, and so the men of Israel retreated.

8663.label: 2 Samuel 23:10
8663.text: He it was that rose up and kept striking down the Phi·lisʹtines until his hand wearied and his hand kept cleaving to the sword, so that Jehovah performed a great salvation on that day; and as for the people, they returned behind him only to strip [those struck down].

8664.label: 2 Samuel 23:11
8664.text: And next to him was Shamʹmah the son of Aʹgee the Harʹa·rite. And the Phi·lisʹtines proceeded to gather themselves to Leʹhi, where there then happened to be a tract of the field full of lentils; and the people themselves fled because of the Phi·lisʹtines.

8665.label: 2 Samuel 23:12
8665.text: But he took his stand in the middle of the tract and delivered it and kept striking down the Phi·lisʹtines, so that Jehovah performed a great salvation.

8666.label: 2 Samuel 23:13
8666.text: And three of the thirty head ones proceeded to go down and come at [the] harvest, to David at the cave of A·dulʹlam; and a tent village of the Phi·lisʹtines was encamped in the low plain of the Rephʹa·im.

8667.label: 2 Samuel 23:14
8667.text: And David was then in the place hard to approach; and an outpost of the Phi·lisʹtines was then in Bethʹle·hem.

8668.label: 2 Samuel 23:15
8668.text: After a while David expressed his craving and said: “O that I might have a drink of the water from the cistern of Bethʹle·hem that is at the gate!”

8669.label: 2 Samuel 23:16
8669.text: At that the three mighty men forced their way into the camp of the Phi·lisʹtines and drew water from the cistern of Bethʹle·hem that is at the gate and came carrying and bringing it to David; and he did not consent to drink it, but poured it out to Jehovah.

8670.label: 2 Samuel 23:17
8670.text: And he went on to say: “It is unthinkable on my part, O Jehovah, that I should do this! [Shall I drink] the blood of the men going at the risk of their souls?” And he did not consent to drink it. These are the things the three mighty men did.

8671.label: 2 Samuel 23:18
8671.text: As for A·bishʹai the brother of Joʹab the son of Ze·ruʹiah, he was the head of the thirty, and he was brandishing his spear over three hundred slain ones, and he had a reputation like the three.

8672.label: 2 Samuel 23:19
8672.text: Although he was distinguished even more than the rest of the thirty, and he came to be their chief, to the rank of the [first] three he did not come.

8673.label: 2 Samuel 23:20
8673.text: As for Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da the son of a valiant man, who did many deeds in Kabʹze·el, he himself struck down the two sons of Arʹi·el of Moʹab; and he himself descended and struck down a lion inside a waterpit on a day of snowfall.

8674.label: 2 Samuel 23:21
8674.text: And he it was that struck down the Egyptian man that was of extraordinary size. Though there was a spear in the hand of the Egyptian, yet he went on down to him with a rod and snatched the spear away from the Egyptian’s hand and killed him with his own spear.

8675.label: 2 Samuel 23:22
8675.text: These things Be·naiʹah the son of Je·hoiʹa·da did; and he had a reputation like the three mighty men.

8676.label: 2 Samuel 23:23
8676.text: Although he was distinguished even more than the thirty, to the rank of the three he did not come; but David appointed him to his own bodyguard.

8677.label: 2 Samuel 23:24
8677.text: Asʹa·hel the brother of Joʹab was among the thirty; El·haʹnan the son of Doʹdo of Bethʹle·hem,

8678.label: 2 Samuel 23:25
8678.text: Shamʹmah the Haʹrod·ite, E·liʹka the Haʹrod·ite,

8679.label: 2 Samuel 23:26
8679.text: Heʹlez the Palʹtite, Iʹra the son of Ikʹkesh the Te·koʹite,

8680.label: 2 Samuel 23:27
8680.text: Abi-eʹzer the Anʹa·thoth·ite, Me·bunʹnai the Huʹshath·ite,

8681.label: 2 Samuel 23:28
8681.text: Zalʹmon the A·hoʹhite, Maʹha·rai the Ne·tophʹa·thite,

8682.label: 2 Samuel 23:29
8682.text: Heʹleb the son of Baʹa·nah the Ne·tophʹa·thite, Itʹtai the son of Riʹbai of Gibʹe·ah of the sons of Benjamin,

8683.label: 2 Samuel 23:30
8683.text: Be·naiʹah a Pirʹa·thon·ite, Hidʹdai of the torrent valleys of Gaʹash,

8684.label: 2 Samuel 23:31
8684.text: Aʹbi-alʹbon the Arʹbath·ite, Azʹma·veth the Bar-huʹmite,

8685.label: 2 Samuel 23:32
8685.text: E·liʹah·ba the Sha·alʹbo·nite, the sons of Jaʹshen, Jonʹa·than,

8686.label: 2 Samuel 23:33
8686.text: Shamʹmah the Harʹa·rite, A·hiʹam the son of Shaʹrar the Harʹa·rite,

8687.label: 2 Samuel 23:34
8687.text: E·liphʹe·let the son of A·hasʹbai the son of the Ma·acʹa·thite, E·liʹam the son of A·hithʹo·phel the Giʹlon·ite,

8688.label: 2 Samuel 23:35
8688.text: Hezʹro the Carʹmel·ite, Paʹa·rai the Arʹbite,

8689.label: 2 Samuel 23:36
8689.text: Iʹgal the son of Nathan of Zoʹbah, Baʹni the Gadʹite,

8690.label: 2 Samuel 23:37
8690.text: Zeʹlek the Amʹmon·ite, Naʹha·rai the Be·erʹoth·ite, armor-bearers of Joʹab the son of Ze·ruʹiah,

8691.label: 2 Samuel 23:38
8691.text: Iʹra the Ithʹrite, Gaʹreb the Ithʹrite,

8693.label: 2 Samuel 24:1
8693.text: And again the anger of Jehovah came to be hot against Israel, when one incited David against them, saying: “Go, take a count of Israel and Judah.”

8694.label: 2 Samuel 24:2
8694.text: So the king said to Joʹab the chief of the military forces who was with him: “Move about, please, through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beʹer-sheʹba, and YOU men register the people, and I shall certainly know the number of the people.”

8695.label: 2 Samuel 24:3
8695.text: But Joʹab said to the king: “May Jehovah your God even add to the people a hundred times as many as they are while the very eyes of my lord the king are seeing it. But as for my lord the king, why has he found delight in this thing?”

8696.label: 2 Samuel 24:4
8696.text: Finally the king’s word prevailed upon Joʹab and the chiefs of the military forces. So Joʹab and the chiefs of the military forces went out from before the king to register the people Israel.

8697.label: 2 Samuel 24:5
8697.text: Then they crossed the Jordan and took up camping at A·roʹer to the right of the city that is in the middle of the torrent valley, toward the Gadʹites, and to Jaʹzer.

8698.label: 2 Samuel 24:6
8698.text: After that they came on to Gilʹe·ad and the land of Tahʹtim-hodʹshi and continued on to Dan-jaʹan and went around to Siʹdon.

8699.label: 2 Samuel 24:7
8699.text: Then they came to the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hiʹvites and of the Caʹnaan·ites and came to the terminating point in the Negʹeb of Judah at Beʹer-sheʹba.

8700.label: 2 Samuel 24:8
8700.text: Thus they went moving about through all the land and came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

8701.label: 2 Samuel 24:9
8701.text: Joʹab now gave the number of the registration of the people to the king; and Israel amounted to eight hundred thousand valiant men drawing sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

8702.label: 2 Samuel 24:10
8702.text: And David’s heart began to beat him after he had so numbered the people. Consequently David said to Jehovah: “I have sinned very much in what I have done. And now, Jehovah, let your servant’s error pass by, please; for I have acted very foolishly.”

8703.label: 2 Samuel 24:11
8703.text: When David proceeded to rise up in the morning, Jehovah’s word itself came to Gad the prophet, David’s visionary, saying:

8704.label: 2 Samuel 24:12
8704.text: “Go, and you must say to David, ‘This is what Jehovah has said: “Three things I am laying upon you. Choose for yourself one of them that I may do it to you.”’”

8705.label: 2 Samuel 24:13
8705.text: Accordingly Gad came in to David and told him and said to him: “Should there come to you seven years of famine in your land, or three months of your fleeing before your adversaries, with them pursuing you, or the occurring of three days of pestilence in your land? Now know and see what I shall reply to the One sending me.”

8706.label: 2 Samuel 24:14
8706.text: So David said to Gad: “It is very distressing to me. Let us fall, please, into the hand of Jehovah, for many are his mercies; but into the hand of man do not let me fall.”

8707.label: 2 Samuel 24:15
8707.text: Then Jehovah gave a pestilence in Israel from the morning until the time appointed, so that out of the people from Dan to Beʹer-sheʹba seventy thousand persons died.

8708.label: 2 Samuel 24:16
8708.text: And the angel kept his hand thrust out toward Jerusalem to bring it to ruin; and Jehovah began to feel regret over the calamity, and so he said to the angel that was bringing ruin among the people: “It is enough! Now let your hand drop.” And Jehovah’s angel himself happened to be close by the threshing floor of A·rauʹnah the Jebʹu·site.

8709.label: 2 Samuel 24:17
8709.text: And David proceeded to say to Jehovah, when he saw the angel that was striking the people down, yes, he proceeded to say: “Here it is I that have sinned and it is I that have done wrong; but these sheep —what have they done? Let your hand, please, come upon me and upon the house of my father.”

8710.label: 2 Samuel 24:18
8710.text: Later Gad came in to David on that day and said to him: “Go up, set up for Jehovah an altar on the threshing floor of A·rauʹnah the Jebʹu·site.”

8711.label: 2 Samuel 24:19
8711.text: And David began to go up in accord with the word of Gad, according to what Jehovah had commanded.

8712.label: 2 Samuel 24:20
8712.text: When A·rauʹnah looked down and saw the king and his servants passing along toward him, A·rauʹnah at once went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the earth.

8713.label: 2 Samuel 24:21
8713.text: Then A·rauʹnah said: “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” At that David said: “To buy from you the threshing floor for building an altar to Jehovah, that the scourge may be halted from upon the people.”

8714.label: 2 Samuel 24:22
8714.text: But A·rauʹnah said to David: “Let my lord the king take it and offer up what is good in his eyes. See the cattle for the burnt offering and the threshing sledge and the implements of the cattle for the wood.

8715.label: 2 Samuel 24:23
8715.text: Everything A·rauʹnah, O king, does give to the king.” And A·rauʹnah went on to say to the king: “May Jehovah your God show pleasure in you.”

8716.label: 2 Samuel 24:24
8716.text: However, the king said to A·rauʹnah: “No, but without fail I shall buy it from you for a price; and I shall not offer up to Jehovah my God burnt sacrifices without cost.” Accordingly David bought the threshing floor and the cattle for fifty silver shekels.

8717.label: 2 Samuel 24:25
8717.text: And David proceeded to build there an altar to Jehovah and offer up burnt sacrifices and communion sacrifices, and Jehovah began letting himself be entreated for the land, so that the scourge was halted from upon Israel.
